The M2 datasets fill a 17-dimensional box of TGLF inputs uniformly, and most of the box lies
far above the instability threshold, where turbulent fluxes are large ([entry 17](17-tglf-datasets-mastu-iter.qmd)).
A transport solver is most sensitive near the threshold, where the flux turns on. The brief
asks for active learning there; the owner moved it to after the first surrogates ([OQ-18](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-18)), so
the ensemble of [entry 18](18-tglf-surrogates-baseline.qmd) could choose the points.

## Selection

For each machine we drew a pool of 10^6^ points from the same approved region as v1, with new
seeds, and scored every point with the TGLF-NN ensemble:
$s = \sigma\,\exp\!\left(-|\mathrm{symlog}(\hat Q_e + \hat Q_i)|/2\right)$, where $\sigma$ is
the members' disagreement on $Q_e$ and $Q_i$ and the exponential is largest where the predicted
heat flux is near zero. The selected batch (v2-al) is 10^5^ points drawn with probability
proportional to $s$; a control batch (v2-random) is 10^5^ other pool points drawn uniformly. A
first score, $\sigma(1 + \text{proximity})$, was dropped before any TGLF run: on a test pool
its picks followed $\sigma$ alone, which is largest far above threshold. TGLF labelled both
batches: [4 × 10^5^ cases, all completed with finite fluxes; 1 h 16 min (MAST-U) and 1 h 15 min (ITER)]{.claim}[C-090](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-090){.cid .st-measured}.

The selection moved the data towards threshold. By TGLF's own $Q_e + Q_i$, below 1 gB / 1-100
gB / above 10^4^ gB: [MAST-U 16% / 18% / 28% in v1 against 45% / 31% / 5% in the selected batch; ITER 17% / 39% / 10% against 35% / 47% / 2%]{.claim}[C-091](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-091){.cid .st-measured}.

## Retraining against a uniform batch

We trained the TGLF-NN ensemble three ways per machine: on v1, on v1 plus the selected batch,
and on v1 plus the uniform batch. Validation stays on v1; each batch keeps a fixed tenth as a
holdout. The table gives the median relative error of $Q_e$ on the v1 test split / the selected batch's holdout / the
uniform batch's holdout.

| training data | MAST-U | ITER |
|---|---|---|
| v1 only | [0.75 / 0.85 / 0.76]{.claim}[C-093](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-093){.cid .st-measured} | [0.60 / 0.69 / 0.59]{.claim}[C-096](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-096){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 + selected batch | [0.72 / 0.81 / 0.73]{.claim}[C-094](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-094){.cid .st-measured} | [0.57 / 0.64 / 0.55]{.claim}[C-097](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-097){.cid .st-measured} |
| v1 + uniform batch | [0.69 / 0.81 / 0.70]{.claim}[C-095](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-095){.cid .st-measured} | [0.55 / 0.62 / 0.52]{.claim}[C-098](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-098){.cid .st-measured} |

Both batches lower the error, by about what the learning curve gives for the larger training
set ([fit 0.70 (MAST-U) and 0.52 (ITER); measured 0.72 and 0.57 with the selected batch, 0.69 and 0.55 with the uniform batch]{.claim}[C-101](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-101){.cid .st-measured}). The uniform batch lowers it as much or more on every test set,
including the selected batch's own holdout, where the selected-batch model trained on the
same distribution. The differences, uniform minus selected, with paired
bootstrap intervals over test cases: [on the selected batch's holdout 0.000 (-0.013 to 0.009) for MAST-U and -0.015 (-0.028 to -0.003) for ITER; on the v1 test split -0.023 (-0.033 to -0.014) and -0.027 (-0.040 to -0.015)]{.claim}[C-099](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-099){.cid .st-measured}. Near threshold on that holdout, $Q_e$
shows no resolved difference and $Q_i$ favours the uniform batch ([MAST-U Q_e 0.77 against 0.78, Q_i 0.74 against 0.73; ITER Q_e 0.58 against 0.57, Q_i 0.54 against 0.52]{.claim}[C-100](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-100){.cid .st-measured}). Round 1
of active learning did not beat uniform sampling.

Every model does worst on the selected holdout: those cases are harder, and concentrating
data there did not pay for what it took from elsewhere. The disagreement $\sigma$ is a weak
guide to the actual error (rank correlation [0.39-0.51 for the MLP ensemble and 0.53-0.62 for the TGLF-NN network]{.claim}[C-089](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-089){.cid .st-measured}). The check does not depend on
the selecting ensemble: the outcomes are TGLF's fluxes on held-out cases.

## Decision OQ-19

With uniform sampling, the measured slopes put a median error of 0.30 at [about 3 × 10^6^ cases (ITER) and about 10^9^ (MAST-U)]{.claim}[C-084](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-084){.cid .st-preliminary}.
[OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) settles three points; the owner left the first two to the agent's recommendation and
asked for the third:

1. **Dataset v3** samples where the coupled simulation goes: TGLF inputs from TORAX states
   along trajectories over a family of scenarios per machine, gradients perturbed around each
   state, and the geometry from the same equilibrium (lifting [K-018](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-018) for v3). MAST-U profiles
   are simulated, not measured.
2. **Accuracy target**: median relative error of the ensemble mean at most 0.30 on $Q_e$ and
   on $Q_i$ ($|Q| > 1$ gB), on each machine's v3 test split.
3. **ReLU on the heat-flux outputs**: zero below threshold and no negative heat flux. TGLF's
   own fluxes are negative in a minority of cases, [Q_e < 0 in 2.0-6.5% of cases (below -1 gB in 0.5-1.5%; median of the negative values -0.03 to -0.09 gB); Q_i < 0 in 9.4-14.1% (below -1 gB in 2.2-5.1%); particle fluxes negative in 33-54%]{.claim}[C-102](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-102){.cid .st-measured}; the ReLU sets those
   heat fluxes to zero, and the particle fluxes keep their sign.

M3 is in progress: dataset v3 and the ReLU outputs are next.
